title: A single perfect weak generator for an algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$, with its small etale site and structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $D(\mathcal O_X)$ for the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for its full subcategory of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology. A perfect object means one etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover, and its diagonal is quasi-compact. There is a perfect object $P\in C_X$ such that, for every $E\in C_X$, $E\cong0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(P[n],E)=0$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-distinguished-square-induction] to the isomorphism-invariant property that $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ admits a perfect object detecting zero by all shifted Hom groups. We verify its affine case and its elementary-square implication below. In the latter implication write $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$, $f:V\to Y$, and $W=U\times_YV$; $Y$ is quasi-compact quasi-separated, $U$ is quasi-compact and $V$ is affine. The induction principle ensures all four vertices are in its quasi-compact quasi-separated domain. Its hypotheses include the property for $U,V,W$; only that for $U$ will be needed.

For affine $Y$, take a scheme perfect generator from [lem-pc-perfect-generator-exists]. The weak-generator definition [def-pc-generators] says that vanishing of all shifted Hom groups forces zero: rewrite $\operatorname{Hom}(P,E[m])$ as $\operatorname{Hom}(P[-m],E)$. Pass to the small etale site by [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence]; full faithfulness and compatibility with shifts preserve these Hom groups and zero objects. Perfectness is preserved by [lem-sfb-etale-detects-perfect]. This proves the affine case, including the empty affine scheme. We use the existing scheme theorem rather than reintroducing its affine special case.

source.place: Tag 09IY, affine paragraph; scheme theorem Tag 09IS.

proof.text: In the elementary square, choose a perfect weak generator $P$ on $U$ using the inductive hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-open-retract] to get a perfect $Q$ on $Y$ and maps $P\xrightarrow{i}Q|_U\xrightarrow{r}P$ with $ri=1$. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The open $W\subset V$ is quasi-compact. Its complement is $V(I)$ for an ideal $I\subset A$; the opens $D(a)$, $a\in I$, cover $W$ by the definition of $V(I)$. Choose a finite subcover $D(a_1),\ldots,D(a_t)$. Thus $V\setminus W=V(a_1,\ldots,a_t)$. Let $K$ be the etale realization of the finite Koszul complex on these elements. It is a bounded finite-free complex, hence perfect by the local definition. It vanishes on $W$ by [lem-pc-koszul-restriction-zero] and the derived etale comparison, so is supported on $f^{-1}(Y\setminus U)$.

By [lem-sfb-space-supported-etale-excision], $K^{\prime}=Rf_*K$ agrees with $f_!K$, restricts to $K$ on $V$, and restricts to zero on $U$. Both restrictions are perfect. Since $U\amalg V\to Y$ is an etale cover, the local definition [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] makes $K^{\prime}$ perfect (the argument of Tag 08HK). Put $G=Q\oplus K^{\prime}$. Finite direct sums of the bounded local finite-projective representatives are again such representatives, after refining the two local covers, so $G$ is perfect. Since $Y$ is qcqs, the quasi-coherent-cohomology clause of [lem-sfb-space-perfect-objects-compact] gives $G\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. Suppose $E$ belongs to this category and $\operatorname{Hom}(G[n],E)=0$ for all $n$. The inclusions and projections of the summands give $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[n],E)=\operatorname{Hom}(K^{\prime}[n],E)=0$. Apply the Hom bijection in the excision statement with $M=E$ and integer $-n$, and move the shift from the target to the source: $\operatorname{Hom}(K^{\prime}[n],E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K[n],f^*E)$.

source.place: Tag 09IY, construction of Q plus K prime and first Hom formula.

proof.text: The etale restriction $E|_V$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. Apply [lem-pc-perfect-generation-koszul-orthogonal] on the Zariski affine scheme $V$, taking its ambient scheme $X=V$ and open $U=W$ (so $X=U\cup V$). All its hypotheses hold, especially the quasi-compactness of $W$. The equivalence [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] preserves the Koszul complex, restriction, shifted Hom and the derived pushforward along $h:W\hookrightarrow V$. Hence its conclusion on the etale site is that the canonical unit $E|_V\to Rh_*(E|_W)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09IY, use of orthogonal Koszul complexes, Tag 09IR.

proof.text: We now supply the omitted detail. Consider the canonical unit $\eta:E\to Rj_*j^*E$. On $U$ it is the identity under $j^*Rj_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$: etale base change for the open $j$ gives this identification, since $U\times_YU=U$. On $V$, etale base change identifies $f^*Rj_*j^*E$ with $Rh_*(E|_W)$ and identifies $f^*\eta$ with the unit of the preceding step, because [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] respects units. Thus $\eta$ is an isomorphism on both members of the jointly surjective etale cover $U\amalg V\to Y$. Its cone has zero cohomology on that cover; a sheaf whose restrictions vanish on a cover is zero by the sheaf axiom. Consequently the cone is acyclic and $\eta$ is an isomorphism globally. In particular $E\simeq Rj_*(E|_U)$.

source.place: Tag 09IY, sentence This implies that E equals R(U to X) star E restricted to U (small detail omitted).

proof.text: Using $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ from [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] and $E\simeq Rj_*E|_U$, we have $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[n],E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q|_U[n],E|_U)=0$. Given $a:P[n]\to E|_U$, the composite $a r[n]$ is zero; composing with $i[n]$ gives $a=0$ since $ri=1$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(P[n],E|_U)=0$ for every $n$. The inductive detection property of $P$ yields $E|_U=0$, and the unit isomorphism gives $E=Rj_*0=0$. Conversely every map to a zero object is zero. This completes the elementary-square implication and therefore the induction in step 1.

source.place: Tag 09IY, final paragraph and final Hom formula.
